subject: ventures/league-schedule-generator
professional: a league commissioner / sports scheduler who builds round-robin fixtures for rec and youth leagues (with a combinatorics-minded second reader familiar with the circle method and de Werra's break-minimisation result): first checks are that every pair meets the right number of times, byes are one per team in odd leagues, home/away breaks hit the known minimum, and that blackouts, skipped dates and courts are honoured on real dates

evidence.correctness: Wrote my own checker (session scratchpad: rr.mjs, bs.mjs, st.mjs) that imports calc.mjs and recomputes from the output, not from the author's tests. (1) Circle-method structure, `roundRobin(n,{double})` for n in 3,4,5,...,14,16,20, single and double: every unordered pair meets exactly once (twice for double), game count equals n(n-1)/2 (x2), no team appears twice in a round, a bye is present exactly when n is odd and each team gets exactly 1 bye (2 in double). All 56 cases pass. (2) Home/away: I counted consecutive same-venue games per team myself. Even n single round robin gives n-2 breaks (n=4: 2, 6: 4, 8: 6, 10: 8, 12: 10, 14: 12, 16: 14, 20: 18), the de Werra minimum the README claims; home-game spread is 1 (unavoidable with n-1 odd games) and 0 in double. For odd n `countBreaks` reports 0 (single), and treats a bye as resetting the streak, which the code comment says; counting across the bye (my definition) odd n single is also 0, but odd-n double counts n breaks by my method against n-2 by the tool, because the bye separates the two legs' joint. Double round robin even n: 3(n-2) (n=6: 12, n=8: 18, n=16: 42), matching the README's 'mirrored double round robin has 3 x (n - 2)'. (3) End-to-end `buildSchedule` on 7 teams, double, Tuesday start 2026-10-06, skip 2026-11-03, team C blacked out 2026-10-20, 3 courts: 14 rounds, 42 matches (expected 7x6), every ordered pair exactly once, all dates Tuesdays, nothing on the skipped date, C plays nothing on its blackout, no team twice on a night, home count 6 for every team, and `validateSchedule` returns ok. (4) `standings` on a 4-team, 6-result league: points/GD for Hawks 6/+3, Lynx 5/+1, Owls 4/+2, Bears 1/-6 match my hand table (3-1-0, order by points). Not recomputed: simulated-annealing court/time-slot balance (seeded, only validated), the multi-division engine (divisions.mjs, 1843 lines) beyond the repo's own tests, rainout movers, exports (.ics, CSV) against a live calendar.
evidence.completeness: Checked README feature claims by calling the code: single/double round robin with byes (works, above); real dates, weekday, skip dates, team blackouts with makeup rounds (works in my run; no makeup needed there, existing tests cover makeup); courts/time slots (works); standings with points, GD and head-to-head, `parseResults` (works); the 32 guide pages and the three tables ('round-robin-schedule-by-number-of-teams', 'template', bracket table) exist as files and are recomputed by page.test.mjs; server.mjs plus its tests, Dockerfile, fly.toml, render.yaml, docker-compose.yml exist. The README is a very long feature log (one bullet runs to several hundred words, with measured experiment results inline), which makes it hard to tell what is core. Several items are self-disclosed as not exercised against reality: Google/Outlook calendar CSV 'not tried against a live account', multi-division season-grid page button 'not clicked in a browser', rest gaps 'no real league checked'. I did not run `eval/browser-click.mjs` (needs Playwright and Chromium) or load any page in a browser, so page behaviour is taken from the test suite (page.test.mjs, 854 lines) and the project's own record. No TODO/FIXME in *.mjs.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/league-schedule-generator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 366 tests, 366 pass, 0 fail, 55 s. Seeded mutations in `roundRobin` (calc.mjs), each reverted with `git checkout calc.mjs`, `git status --short ventures/league-schedule-generator` clean afterwards: (a) pairing arithmetic `(r - k + (N - 1)) % (N - 1)` changed to `(r - k + (N - 2)) % (N - 1)`: `node --test calc.test.mjs` -> 130 pass, 49 FAIL, caught; (b) home/away alternation `k % 2 === 1` changed to `k % 2 === 2` (never alternates): `node --test calc.test.mjs page.test.mjs` -> 206 pass, 25 FAIL, caught. The suite recomputes the published tables from the engine, validates every length 3 to 14 teams, and the repo ships mutation scripts (eval/mutate-validator.mjs, eval/mutate-divisions.mjs) and fuzzers (eval/fuzz-*.mjs), which I did not run. Weak spot worth noting: the guide-page tests recompute tables from the same `roundRobin`, so they confirm page and code agree, not that the code is right; the independent check is the validator, and the circle method itself is only pinned by structural properties plus hand-computed 4- and 5-team leagues. Two mutations only (both in the round-robin core); I did not mutate standings, the date planner, or the rainout mover.
evidence.craft: Read: calc.mjs roundRobin, countBreaks, buildSchedule head (lines ~355-520, 619-660), standings head, the first 120 lines of the README, file inventory. Good: the circle method is a clean 12-line function; seeded mulberry32 PRNG makes output reproducible; an independent `validateSchedule` re-checks a finished schedule; input errors are thrown with readable messages (team limits, courts x slots too small); the project ships fuzzers and mutation scripts. Defects: calc.mjs is a 3,197-line single module mixing round robin, annealing, rainouts, Swiss, Americano, brackets, officials, CSV/ICS exports and cost maths; divisions.mjs is another 1,843 lines; page logic is in HTML (not read). A senior reviewer would split it. The README is an unstructured changelog with inline experiment write-ups, not documentation. `countBreaks` takes a schedule shaped differently from the `roundRobin` output (it needs {teams, rounds:[{matches:[{home,away}]}]} while roundRobin returns [h,a] pairs), a trap I hit when reusing it. sitemap.xml lists relative URLs. Time-slot/court annealing is stochastic, so 'same seed same schedule' is the only stability guarantee.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'home and away balanced (the minimum possible breaks)' - true for even n single round robin (n-2, verified), but for a double round robin the engine mirrors the first leg and has 3(n-2) breaks; the README discloses 3 x (n-2) in the home/away guide bullet but the headline 'minimum possible' is not qualified, and a non-mirrored second leg can do better (the how-to page itself states the mirrored figure). 'Nothing is uploaded' / browser-only: matches an HTML+mjs design and the share link in the URL fragment (not network-tested here). 'Tested against hand-computed 4- and 5-team leagues and a seeded random check of every size from 2 to 24 teams': the suite and fuzz-build.test.mjs exist; I did not re-run the 2-24 sweep specifically. No-warranty and 'check every date, court and pairing' text present in README; index.html contains disclaimer wording. Per-feature measured numbers in the README (e.g. '176 -> 395 breaks', '17 nights -> 13', '-6.7%') come from eval scripts and are not reproducible from a one-line command in the README; I did not reproduce them. Problems: llms.txt links the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host as the live tool and pages (lines 9-11) although the live site is marisstella.app (the README itself says so); sitemap.xml uses relative <loc> values ('./index.html'), which the sitemap protocol does not allow (absolute URLs required), so it gives search engines nothing as committed unless a build step rewrites it, which I did not find; README 'Tools' line says 'Open index.html. No build step' while also documenting a Node server with admin keys, so the two products are mixed in one README.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a commissioner of a 7-team Tuesday league wants a double round robin from 2026-10-06 with a holiday skip and one team's unavailable night, 3 fields. buildSchedule produced a valid, complete 14-night fixture list with real dates, all constraints met and balanced home games (6 each) in one call; standings from typed results are right; the CSV/ICS/text exports and the print stylesheet exist. Gaps a commissioner would hit: no hosted check that the live page works (not loaded here); the double round robin has 3(n-2) home/away breaks where many leagues expect a non-mirrored second half; a very long single-file feature surface may overwhelm a casual organiser; mobile use not tested; no outside user is recorded in this audit. For the stated user (a volunteer organiser) the core job is done well.
evidence.domain: Compared against the circle (polygon) method and de Werra's result that an even round robin can have as few as n-2 breaks (the engine reaches n-2, verified for n=4..20) and the standard bye handling for odd n (one bye per team, verified). A scheduler would also look at: break-minimised or 'carryover'-balanced orderings (not offered; not claimed), mirrored versus non-mirrored (French/Spanish) second legs (only mirrored is built, honestly disclosed), unrelated venue-availability constraints (courts, closures, linked teams, shared grounds are all handled), and tiebreaks (points, GD, GF, optional head-to-head; ordering by head-to-head before GD is a league-rules choice the page leaves to the organiser). Departures: points-per-game is not used when teams played unequal games (the README notes this for shorter seasons); first-leg/second-leg phasing is fixed. Practitioners would sign off on the method with those limits.

defects.what: sitemap.xml lists relative URLs (<loc>./index.html</loc> and so on). The sitemap protocol requires absolute URLs, so the committed file does nothing for SEO; I found no build step in the venture that rewrites it.

Headline claim 'home and away balanced (the minimum possible breaks)' is not qualified for a double round robin: the engine mirrors leg one and yields 3(n-2) breaks (verified n=6: 12, n=8: 18), whereas the minimum is lower with a non-mirrored second leg. Disclosed deep in the home/away guide bullet, not in the opening claim. With odd n, `countBreaks` resets the streak at a bye, so double-round-robin odd leagues report n-2 breaks while games on either side of the bye keep the same venue in n of the sequences by a straight count.
llms.txt links the retired duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo host as the live tool and guides; the live address is marisstella.app/league-schedule-generator/ (as the README says).

calc.mjs (3,197 lines) and divisions.mjs (1,843 lines) are monoliths holding unrelated domains (round robin, annealing, Swiss, Americano, brackets, officials, costs, exports). The README is a feature log with long inline experiment write-ups rather than structured docs, and mixes the browser tool with the self-hosted server.

Guide-page tests recompute worked tables from the same roundRobin that generates them, so they prove page-code agreement, not independent correctness; countBreaks takes a differently shaped schedule from roundRobin's output, an easy misuse.

Several README features are self-declared as untested against the real thing (Google/Outlook CSV not tried against a live account; multi-division grid button not clicked; rest gaps tested on a made-up league only). I did not run the Playwright browser eval, so page behaviour is unverified by me.
defects.where: ventures/league-schedule-generator/README.md (Calendar CSV, Multi-division season grid, Rest gaps bullets)

verdict: A solid, honestly self-limited scheduling tool whose core is right: I recomputed round-robin structure for 14 team counts (single and double), home/away breaks (n-2 even single, 3(n-2) mirrored double, matching the README), bye handling (one per team for odd n), an end-to-end 7-team double schedule with a skipped date and a blackout, and a 4-team standings table, all against my own independent code and hand tables, with no discrepancy. The 366-test suite passes and two seeded mutations in the circle-method core were caught (49 and 25 failures). It meets the bar on correctness, verification and median, but claims is 2 (relative-URL sitemap, an llms.txt pointing at a retired host, an unqualified 'minimum possible breaks' headline that only holds for single even leagues) and craft is 2 (3,000-line monolith, changelog README). Because claims is below 3 it does not meet the bar as computed, even though the maths is sound and the project is finished (completeness 3). Not run: the Playwright browser eval, the fuzzers and the annealing quality; scores reflect only what was run. Cheapest fixes: absolute sitemap URLs, repoint llms.txt, qualify the double round robin claim.
